text:
Tom: FYI perf alert — throughput on gpu-pool-prod-r4 down ~35% since 02:10 UTC, spike of OOMs on 3 workers. Rolling back runtime commit rfe/kv-prefetch-17 reverted? Any ideas?
Maya: looking now, attaching tail of allocator logs, seeing repeated slab evict -> slow_kern fallback
OpsBot: alert: GPU-OOM spike (3 hosts) - incident created #INC-2345
Liam: re: kernels, I just rolled the kernel-selection tweak at 01:45 — meant to prefer fastpath for seq<=512, but heuristic appears inverted for mixed-batch sizes. Could be picking slow_kernel for seq<64 unintentionally.
Maya: that matches allocation pattern — small seqs causing high per-request overhead -> more KV cache allocations -> fragmentation
Anita: quick profiling snapshot (ptop):
```
kernel_choice: slow_kernel 67%
fast_kernel: 22%
allocator.nmalloc: 480k
kv_evictions/sec: 12.4
latency_p95: 420ms -> 680ms
```
Jordan: noisy tenant on t-tenant-12 had heavy short-queries at 02:05, likely thrashing KV cache
Tom: can we flip kernel heuristic back?
Liam: yes, pushing hotfix now (will canary to 2 hosts)
Maya: also temp disable prefix KV caching for pool to reduce KV churn (will test)
OpsBot: deploy started: runtime-hotfix/ks-rollback -> canary (2/2 hosts)
Liam: canary rolled, initial metrics look better, p95 back to ~300ms, no new OOMs on canary
Tom: roll full if stable for 15m. Also create follow-up to add unit test for batch-mix heuristic and add metric for "kernel-mismatch-rate"
Anita: added task in #eng-runtime backlog — https://boards/redwood/RT-512
Maya: postmortem notes — likely root cause: inverted threshold in kernel selection logic + KV cache amplification under short-seq noisy tenant -> fragmentation and OOM -> worker restarts causing throughput drop
Tom: thanks all. I'll keep thread open for 30m, file incident after stability
Liam: linking flamegraph: https://perf/redwood/flame/2330123400
Maya: leaving logs in /var/log/runtime/alloc-2330123456.log
Tom: :thumbsup:
